edit.description: pkgManagerGate's five hand-copied keys and the cast that lets the copy be short
the bare-and-called key pins, beside the four they already cover

summary: the bare form of a package-manager builtin derives its gate keys from the gate shellGate built for it, so a key that return gains cannot reach the called form alone

per.section: Derived state is computed, never restated beside its source

acceptance: `pkgManagerGate` composes the callable's gate keys off the gate it already built rather than restating `name`, `when`, `batches`, `run` and `command` behind an `as PkgManagerGate` cast, so a key `shellGate`'s return gains reaches `tscGate` used bare as well as called and the typecheck says so when one is missed; `pnpm tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm test` green with the existing key pins unchanged
notes: `pkgManagerGate` (`src/builtinGates.ts:165`-`:192`) copies five keys onto the callable behind an `as` cast, so nothing holds the copy complete — the shipped blocker carried `batches` across by hand and cited this section at the site. The existing pins cover those five on both forms (`tests/builtinGates.test.ts:1140`), so what is unheld is the next key, which is the type's job: no `tests[]`/`pins[]` line, the check this fix installs is the type.
